added.title: Air Pollution Specialist
added.description:
Job Description And Duties

The Regulatory and Risk Modeling (RRM) Section within the Modeling and Meteorology Branch (MMB) is responsible for conducting the triennial California Air Toxics Assessment (CATA) and maintaining the CATA visualization mapping tool and data portal, as well as providing microscale to statewide air quality and toxics modeling support for the Air Board's various regulatory programs, including the community air protection program, airborne toxic control measures, state implementation plans for lead, NO2, and SO2, the air toxics hot spots program, and emergency response support.

The APS, working as part of a team, will support CATA through preparing and QA/QC'ing model inputs, such as emissions inventory, meteorology, and boundary conditions, conduct air dispersion and chemical transport modeling, investigate emerging air toxics (e.g., PCBTF, EtO, acrolein), translate ambient exposure to estimated cancer risk, analyze model outputs, and summarize findings for both technical and public audiences. In addition, the APS will work closely with lead staff on supporting the day-to-day operation of the High Performance Computing (HPC) Linux modeling cluster CATA modeling relies on. This could include monitoring storage and compute node usage, troubleshooting any issues that may arise, and onboarding new users.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Working Conditions

This position may be eligible for hybrid in-office work and in-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Boards' (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in-person attendance is also required.?

The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position?under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.

added.title: Incidents and Remediation Lead
added.description:
Melbourne | Hybrid working

Get to the root cause. Drive meaningful action. Deliver better customer outcomes.

At Latitude, we make it possible—with financing solutions in the moments that matter. Delivering on that purpose means understanding when things go wrong, putting them right and using what we learn to improve.

We’re looking for an Incidents & Remediation Lead
who combines investigative thinking with the drive to get things done. Someone who can work through complex incidents, challenge the evidence and keep remediation moving through to completion.

About the opportunity

Working within our Money business and reporting to the Head of L1 Risk & Compliance, you’ll lead operational incident and issue management across the division.

You’ll bring together business owners, operational teams, Risk & Compliance and Technology to understand what happened, assess customer impacts and agree on effective remediation. You’ll establish clear ownership and milestones, work through roadblocks and escalate when progress is at risk.

Alongside leading investigations and remediation, you’ll coach Senior Analysts and help leaders see the bigger picture—identifying recurring themes, emerging risks and opportunities to strengthen controls.

Your impact

In this role, you’ll:
Lead complex investigations
—uncover root causes, assess customer impacts and identify systemic issues and control gaps.
Drive remediation to completion
—build practical plans with business owners, set clear accountabilities and keep actions progressing.
Challenge the evidence
—define analytical requirements, interrogate data and customer cohort findings, and identify gaps or anomalies.
Turn findings into insight
—provide clear reporting that helps leaders and risk committees understand trends, make decisions and take action.
Strengthen how we operate
—partner across teams to improve controls, simplify processes and reduce the likelihood of incidents recurring.
Maintain strong governance
—keep accurate, audit-ready records and work with Finance and business owners to track remediation costs, provisions and forecasts.
Build capability
—coach Senior Analysts, guide priorities and strengthen the quality of investigation and remediation work.

What you’ll bring

You’re comfortable getting into the detail while keeping sight of the broader risk picture. You ask thoughtful questions, challenge conclusions constructively and know when an issue needs to be escalated.

You also bring follow-through. You can keep multiple workstreams moving, hold stakeholders accountable and maintain momentum when delivery gets complicated.

We’re looking
for:

At least seven years’ experience in operational risk, incident management, compliance or related work within financial services.
Proven experience leading complex incidents and remediation from investigation through to timely closure.
Strong investigative and root cause analysis skills, with the judgement to assess whether proposed actions address the underlying issues.
Strong data literacy, including the ability to define analysis requirements and assess whether evidence supports decisions.
Sound knowledge of risk and control frameworks, control design and effectiveness, assurance or testing, and the three lines of defence model.
An understanding of regulatory and compliance obligations relevant to financial services across Australia and New Zealand.
Clear communication, stakeholder influencing and coaching skills.
A bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management or a related discipline.
Experience in consumer finance would be highly regarded.

More possibilities for you

You’ll join a close-knit team that values curiosity, collaboration and constructive challenge. Your work will directly influence how we resolve incidents, support affected customers and strengthen risk practices across the Money business.

We make it possible…

To take more time for yourself
—with Take 5
, a bonus week of leave each year once you’ve used your four weeks of annual leave.
To enjoy flexibility and connection
—with hybrid working and Melbourne teams generally spending 2–3 days a week in the office
.
To feel supported
—with Sonder
, providing 24/7 wellbeing and safety support.
To access additional benefits
—through a range of employee and selected partner offers.

Our values— Take Ownership, Pursue Excellence, Win Together and Create Tomorrow
—guide how we work and support each other.

Ready for your next opportunity?

Bring your judgement, curiosity and determination to see things through.

Apply now and help us make it possible.

Successful applicants will be required to complete background checks prior to commencing employment.

added.title: Environmental Data Validator
added.description:
Position Description & Qualifications

Serco is seeking an Environmental Data Review & Validation Chemist
to support the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Laboratory Services and Applied Science Division (LSASD) in Fort Meade, Maryland.

As a member of Serco’s Environmental Service Assistance Team, you will collaborate with EPA scientists and staff to review and validate Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data. Your work will contribute directly to the EPA’s mission of protecting human health and the environment.

Serco offers a collaborative work environment with opportunities to expand your technical knowledge, strengthen your analytical skills, and contribute to meaningful environmental initiatives.

In This Role, You Will

Review and validate organic analytical data, including volatile organic compounds, semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, PCBs, dioxins, and PCB congeners, using applicable EPA National Functional Guidelines and regional standard operating procedures.
Validate metals data generated through inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in accordance with applicable National Functional Guidelines.
Prepare detailed, accurate, and professional reports documenting data-review findings.
Manage and maintain electronic analytical data across multiple platforms.
Monitor workflows, backlogs, deliverables, and performance metrics.
Review standard operating procedures as needed.
Track and analyze key performance indicators to identify trends and support continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you must have:

A bachelor’s degree in chemistry or a related scientific field.
At least one year of experience working in an environmental laboratory or with EPA analytical methods. An advanced degree may substitute for some professional experience.
At least one year of experience reviewing and validating analytical data.
Extensive experience performing gas chromatography (GC) or gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analyses using one or more of the following:
EPA Contract Laboratory Program Statements of Work
EPA SW-846 methods
EPA drinking-water methods
Other applicable organic or inorganic analytical methods

Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365.
The ability to obtain and maintain an EPA Public Trust clearance.
Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills.
A solid background in analyzing and interpreting complex scientific data.

Preferred Qualifications

The following experience and skills are preferred:

At least one year of experience working as an organic or inorganic chemist or laboratory technician.
Experience with laboratory quality-control programs and analytical data review or validation.
Experience reviewing or analyzing one or more of the following:
Dioxins and PCB congeners using high-resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HRGC-MS)
Metals using ICP-AES or ICP-MS
Mercury using cold vapor analysis
Classical inorganic parameters, including hexavalent chromium, total organic carbon, total dissolved solids, total suspended solids, total solids, or cyanide

Experience writing technical reports, data-review narratives, standard operating procedures, or similar scientific documentation.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work extensively at a computer using a monitor and keyboard.
Flexibility to work evenings or weekends when required.

We help our clients deliver vital services more efficiently while increasing the satisfaction of their end customers. added.title: CCR Groundwater & Remediation Supervisor
added.description:
The position is located at 241 Ralph McGill Blvd Atlanta, Georgia. In-office 4 days per week, Mon.-Thurs. *

Job Summary

This position is responsible for directing, planning, developing and managing Georgia Power’s groundwater program strategy for compliance with the federal and state Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) Rule. Additionally, this position represents the Company in influencing and negotiating environmental matters with regulatory agencies, environmental organizations, related industry groups, co-owners, customers, other industries, and the public.

This position provides leadership and direction to the team of geologists, engineers, and scientists responsible for developing, communicating, implementing, and leading CCR groundwater compliance strategies and meeting groundwater compliance obligations for company business units and facilities. Additionally, this person is expected to provide input and advice on groundwater related activities encompassing a broad range of regulatory programs (CERCLA, RCRA, HSRA, Brownfields, etc.).

Job Duties & Responsibilities

Responsible for leading Georgia Power’s current and future CCR groundwater compliance strategy and managing submission of all groundwater compliance and reporting requirements. This also includes obtaining and maintaining appropriate permits, licenses, and approvals which meet regulatory requirements and minimize risks and costs to the Company.
Build and maintain relationships with key business units to implement cost effective groundwater compliance strategies with potential cross media issues relating to water treatment, CCR unit closure activities, etc.
Work with appropriate regulatory agencies and external groups to promote informed, balanced, and science-based regulations and permit requirements.
Provide leadership and direction for contract management, invoice processing, compliance with Supply Chain requirements as it pertains to the issuance of bids, bid evaluations, and contractor selection including Supplier Diversity tracking as part of this process.
Support the Company's environmental policies in all areas relating to groundwater compliance.
Participate or serve in leadership roles in internal as well as external organizations to maintain partnerships which foster positive relationships within the company, as well as governmental agencies.
Monitor environmental legislative and regulatory activities that impact company operations industry groups, and public interest groups.

JOB REQUIREMENTS:
(Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills )

Bachelor's degree in, geology, engineering, or a science related field with equivalent work-related experience is required. Professional accreditations and certifications (PG or PE) preferred.
Experience managing groundwater monitoring programs, environmental investigations, remediation, corrective action, or related environmental programs. Ability to interpret and apply complex environmental requirements and develop effective compliance strategies. Direct experience with federal or state CCR Rule requirements is preferred.
Comprehensive knowledge of state and federal environmental laws and regulations, direct experience working with leadership and technical staffs of regulatory agencies, and experience working with external advocacy groups.
Strong technical writing and verbal communication skills; able to synthesize technical information and communicate in a manner suitable for technical and non-technical personnel.
Demonstrated ability to lead technical professionals, establish priorities, communicate expectations, and deliver results. Relevant leadership experience may include direct supervision, project or program leadership, mentoring or oversight of multidisciplinary teams and consultants. Prior people management experience is preferred.
Excellent interpersonal, communication and leadership skills with the ability to negotiate and influence.
Demonstrate strong problem solving and analytical skills and ability to troubleshoot complex problems.

added.title: Sr. Environmental Analyst
added.description:
Position Description

Seattle Public Utilities (SPU) is seeking a highly skilled and detail-oriented Senior Environmental Analyst
to join the Environmental Stewardship and Compliance Division. This critical position provides oversight of the division's environmental data quality, reporting, and regulatory compliance efforts, ensuring the accuracy, integrity, and effectiveness of information used to demonstrate compliance with key environmental regulations, including the City’s Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) NPDES permit and Wastewater Collection System NPDES permit.

About Seattle Public Utilities:
Seattle Public Utilities (SPU) is a community-centered utility that delivers vital services to Seattle residents and businesses including drinking water, drainage and wastewater, and garbage/recycling/compost. SPU also provides drinking water for 1.6 million customers in the region. SPU’s work includes system maintenance and improvements and keeping Seattle clean. Over 1,500 SPU employees work with our community to provide affordable and equitable stewardship of our water and waste resources for future generations.

For more information about Seattle Public Utilities (SPU), check out the:

SPU Website
SPU Workplace Expectations
Strategic Business Plan

SPU commits to Our City Values and Race and Social Justice as core principles that guide our work. We actively take steps to dismantle systemic racism and increase service equity. We value diverse life experiences and strive to create a workplace that is welcoming to all. We take steps to be inclusive and equitable in our recruiting, hiring and promotional opportunities.

Why join us?

About

We know work isn’t only about what you do, it’s also about who you work for and with! SPU provides a fun and family-friendly work environment that supports a work life balance, including:

Hybrid work schedule opportunities
Family-friendly and multicultural work environment
Generous benefits package
Free Orca Pass
City pension plan with employer/employee contributions
Growth potential and advancement opportunities

Job Responsibilities

Lead environmental data management efforts, ensuring data quality, accessibility, and consistency across division programs.
Support compliance with NPDES permits, sediment remediation requirements, and other environmental regulations.
Provide technical expertise in stormwater source control, environmental investigations, sampling, and water quality compliance.
Develop and maintain QAPPs, SOPs, and other quality assurance protocols supporting legally defensible environmental data collection.
Manage, analyze, interpret, and report environmental data to support compliance, investigations, and program decision-making.
Develop and maintain dashboards, KPIs, and performance metrics to evaluate regulatory compliance and program effectiveness.
Maintain specialized environmental databases and ensure the integrity of complex environmental datasets.
Research regulatory trends and industry best practices and recommend process improvements.
Collaborate with internal and external partners on environmental programs, pilot projects, and compliance initiatives.
Support the development and optimization of data systems, software platforms, and business processes.
May assist and participate in spill response activities.

Please note this job advertisement is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job.

Qualifications

Experience
: Five (5) years’ experience in environmental research, environmental law, impact analysis, environmental compliance, toxic substance management, or a related field.

Education:
Bachelor's degree in natural or physical sciences, environmental sciences, planning (with emphasis on environmental issues), public administration/policy (with emphasis on natural resources), or related field.

Experience and Education Equivalency:
Other combinations of education, training and experience will be evaluated on an individual basis for comparability.

Licensing And/or Other Requirements

Current State of Washington driver license
Hazardous materials/toxics work may require specialized health & safety training and certification.

Desired Qualifications

Experience with stormwater source control, environmental investigations, sampling, and data analysis.
Experience developing and implementing environmental QA/QC standards and data management practices.
Knowledge of environmental regulations, including the Clean Water Act, NPDES permits, MTCA, and CERCLA.
Experience with hazardous and dangerous waste identification, management, and regulatory compliance.
Ability to provide technical expertise in environmental compliance, enforcement support, and risk assessment.
Strong technical writing, reporting, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience using performance data to drive process improvements and reduce regulatory risk.
Experience leading projects and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams.
Proficiency with GIS and consultant/vendor contract management.

Additional Information

Work Environment/Physical Demands

Occasional exposure to hazardous waste, chemicals, and other conditions requiring safety precautions.
Hybrid: This position allows for the flexibility of a hybrid work schedule. City employees may have the option to work remotely two days per week. Individual schedules will be agreed upon by the employee and their supervisor.

Who may apply:
The City of Seattle encourages people of all backgrounds to apply, including people of color, immigrants, refugees, women, LGBTQ, people with disabilities, veterans, and those with diverse life experience. This position is open to all qualified candidates that meet the minimum qualifications. The City of Seattle values diverse perspectives and life experiences. Applicants will be considered regardless of race, color, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, disability, religious or political affiliation, age, sexual orientation, or gender identity.

The full salary for this position is $58.21 - $67.84 per hour.

How To Apply

A full City of Seattle online application
In addition to fully completing the online application. please attach your resume and cover letter. Your cover letter should address your knowledge and experience related to the position. If you do not attach these documents, you will no longer be considered.

For more information regarding this recruitment, please contact: Dominic Sumlin at
Dominic.Sumlin@seattle.gov

Benefits:
The City of Seattle offers a comprehensive benefits package including vacation, holiday, and sick leave as well as medical, dental, vision, life and long-term disability insurance for employees and their dependents .

More information about employee benefits is available on the City's website at: https://www.seattle.gov/human-resources/benefits

Learn more about Seattle Public Utilities at www.seattle.gov/util/ and check us out on social media.

added.title: Environmental Data Validation Chemist
added.description:
Position Description & Qualifications

Serco is seeking an Environmental Data Review & Validation Chemist
to support the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Laboratory Services and Applied Science Division (LSASD) in Fort Meade, Maryland.

As a member of Serco’s Environmental Service Assistance Team, you will collaborate with EPA scientists and staff to review and validate Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data. Your work will directly support the EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment.

Serco offers a collaborative work environment with opportunities to expand your technical knowledge, strengthen your analytical skills, and contribute to meaningful environmental initiatives.

In This Role, You Will

Review and validate organic analytical data, including volatile organic compounds, semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, PCBs, dioxins, and PCB congeners, using applicable EPA National Functional Guidelines and regional standard operating procedures.
Validate metals data generated using inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in accordance with applicable National Functional Guidelines.
Prepare detailed, accurate, and professional reports documenting data-review findings.
Manage and maintain electronic analytical data across multiple platforms.
Monitor workflows, backlogs, deliverables, and performance metrics.
Review standard operating procedures as needed.
Track and analyze key performance indicators to identify trends and support continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you must have:

A bachelor’s degree in chemistry or a related scientific field.
Four to seven years of experience working in environmental laboratories or with EPA analytical methods. Advanced education may substitute for some professional experience.
At least five years of experience reviewing and validating analytical data.
Extensive experience performing gas chromatography (GC) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analyses using one or more of the following:
EPA Contract Laboratory Program Statements of Work
EPA SW-846 methods
EPA drinking-water methods
Other applicable organic or inorganic analytical methods

Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365.
The ability to obtain an EPA Public Trust clearance.
Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills.
A solid background in analyzing and interpreting scientific data.

Preferred Qualifications

The following experience and skills are preferred:

At least five years of experience working as an organic or inorganic chemist or laboratory technician.
Experience with laboratory quality-control programs and analytical data review or validation.
Experience reviewing or analyzing one or more of the following:
Dioxins and PCB congeners using high-resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HRGC-MS)
Metals using ICP-AES or ICP-MS
Mercury using cold vapor analysis
Classical inorganic parameters, including hexavalent chromium, total organic carbon, total dissolved solids, total suspended solids, total solids, or cyanide

Experience writing technical reports, data-review narratives, standard operating procedures, or similar scientific documentation.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work extensively at a computer using a monitor and keyboard.
Flexibility to work evenings or weekends when required.

Company Overview

Serco Inc. (Serco) is the Americas division of Serco Group, plc. In North America, Serco’s 9,000+ employees strive to make an impact every day across 100+ sites in the areas of Defense, Citizen Services, and Transportation. We help our clients deliver vital services more efficiently while increasing the satisfaction of their end customers. While your place may look a little different depending on your role, we know you will find yours here. Wherever you work and whatever you do, we invite you to discover your place in our world. Serco is a place you can count on and where you can make an impact because every contribution matters.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking an experienced Program Manager
to support our Oil and Gas business line in Oakland, California. This role will lead the successful delivery of complex environmental projects for clients in the refining, industrial, and related sectors. The selected candidate will oversee one or more projects from planning through execution, providing strategic project leadership, managing risk, ensuring financial performance, and fostering long-term client relationships through the consistent delivery of high-quality project outcomes.

Duties Include But Are Not Limited To

Technical direction and management of staff at a complex petrochemical facility in the San Francisco Bay area.
Serving as the lead interface with clients, community stakeholders, and state and federal agencies.
Delivering projects that meet and exceed schedule and quality requirements.
Managing projects within client budgetary requirements while meeting internal cost and revenue guidelines.
Leading a team that prioritizes safe performance of work.
Managing and mentoring junior and mid-level staff.
Developing work with existing clients through excellence in delivery and building relationships with new clients.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements

Bachelors degree and 8 years of relevant environmental remediation experience (managing sites with complex stakeholder relationship, under jurisdiction of multiple state and federal agencies, at facilities subject to RCRA permits, etc.) or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
Successful candidate mustpass client required drug screening and background check.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
US citizenship or permanent residency required.

Preferred Qualifications

15+ years of environmental consulting experience supporting oil & gas, refining, industrial, or energy-sector clients.
Proven track record managing complex, multi-disciplinary environmental projects with responsibility for scope, schedule, budget, and quality performance.
Strong client relationship management skills with experience growing key accounts and securing repeat business.
Experience leading project teams, mentoring project managers, and managing project risk, contracts, and financial performance.
Professional certification or registration preferred, such as PG, PE, CHMM, PMP, or a related credential.
